findings.issue: The hero's lead, about 40 words, sits on the photo. At 390 px it runs five centred lines under the two-line title and covers the frame from top to bottom, so the photo shows only as a dark texture behind text. At 1440 px it fills the band under the title too.
findings.reference: The competitor's matching page puts only its bold title on the photo, with no lead, and starts its running text under the photo band on white.
findings.fix: Apply the template's rule that a hero lead much longer than the competitor's stands under the hero. Here that means rendering .page-hero__lead under the banner, as the page lead on white, and keeping only the H1 on the photo; heroText.leadWords should not let a 40-word lead onto the photo.

findings.issue: The ten answer cards are solid dark-navy blocks with white text. They form a heavy dark wall of about 1,300 px (3,000 px on phones), and each card's topic ("Certifications", "Lead times" and so on) is set at body size and weight, barely different from the muted "What this means for you" label and the answer under it.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards are light, outlined in 1px (black or #979797) with a 6–10px radius and no fill or shadow. Each card title is bold (700, about 22px) above regular text.
findings.fix: In reference.css, scoped to .block--table[data-variant="cards"] (or the table cards' row class), set the card background to var(--surface-primary), border: 1px solid var(--border-color), border-radius: var(--radius-card) and color: var(--text-primary). Give the topic cell font-weight: 700 and a step-up size from the type scale, leaving the heading fit untouched.

findings.issue: This was raised in the last review and is still open. The process section has no heading: its left column holds only the one body-size line "Quality checks at every stage of an order." beside five steps, between the H2 sections above and below it.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list always opens with an H2 above its lead, in the left column beside the steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give the overview-quality-stages visual (blog.json) a heading, for example "Quality Checks at Every Stage", so the block renders an H2 above the caption.

findings.issue: This is still open from the last review. The three plain sections after the hero (overview, overview-steps, table-1) all sit on white, so nothing but padding separates them.
findings.reference: The site's rule, which follows the competitor's banded pages, is that neighbouring plain sections alternate white and tinted backgrounds.
findings.fix: The template should alternate the plain sections' backgrounds, giving overview-steps var(--section-tint) (the treatment's --surface-secondary #f4eee6) between the white overview and table-1.

findings.issue: The CTA heading "How to Send Your Enquiry Straight to Our Team" is set with a line-height of about 1.4–1.5, against about 1.05 for the H2s above it at the same size. Its three lines drift apart, at 1440 px and at 390 px alike.
findings.reference: The competitor sets every heading level, including its CTA banners, on one tight leading (about 1.1–1.2).
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .cta h2 (the CTA block's heading) the same line-height as the other section headings, about 1.1. Change the leading only, not the fitted font-size.

findings.issue: In the 293 px desktop banner the photo is cropped to a strip of foliage. The person at the right is cut off at the forehead by the top edge, so the band reads as a blurred green texture rather than a picture.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero photo is cropped so its subject (the workshop floor and machines) stays whole and readable behind the title.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set --hero-focal for main[data-page-type="blog_hub"] (for example center 30%) so the crop keeps the person's head and upper body in the band.
